subject: science
cluster: Stars, the Sun, and patterns in the sky
skillName: Patterns in Shadows, Day and Night, and Seasons
intro: Many changes in the sky follow regular, repeating patterns that we can record as data and graph. During a day, a shadow is long in the early morning, shortest around noon when the Sun is highest, and long again in the evening, and the shadow points in different directions as the Sun appears to move across the sky. Day and night repeat because the Earth spins once each day. Across the year, different stars and constellations are visible in the night sky in different seasons, and this pattern repeats every year. Recording and graphing these observations makes the patterns easy to see and lets us predict what will happen.

items.prompt: A student measures the length of a pole's shadow every hour from morning to evening and graphs it. What pattern should the graph show?

steps: In the morning the Sun is low, so shadows are long.
Around noon the Sun is highest, so the shadow is shortest.
In the evening the Sun is low again, so the shadow is long again; the graph should show the shadow shrinking to a shortest point near noon and then growing.
solution.answer: The graph shows the shadow long in the morning, shortest near noon, and long again in the evening.

items.prompt: Why do we have a repeating pattern of day and night?

steps: Day and night depend on whether your side of Earth faces the Sun.
The Earth spins (rotates) once about every 24 hours.
As it spins, each place moves into sunlight (day) and then into shadow (night), repeating every day.
solution.answer: Because the Earth rotates once each day, so each place cycles through day and night.

items.prompt: A student records which constellations are visible at night in winter and in summer and finds they are different. What pattern does this show, and does it repeat?

steps: Different stars are visible at night in different seasons.
This happens as the Earth moves around the Sun over the year.
The pattern repeats: the same seasonal constellations return each year.
solution.answer: Different constellations appear in different seasons, and this pattern repeats every year.

items.prompt: At what time of day is a shadow usually the shortest?

steps: A shadow is shortest when the Sun is highest in the sky.
The Sun is highest around midday, so the shadow is shortest around noon.
solution.answer: Around noon, when the Sun is highest.

items.prompt: A graph shows daylight hours each month: short in winter, longer toward summer, then shorter again. How could this graph help someone predict daylight next year?

steps: The graph shows a smooth, repeating pattern over the months.
Because the pattern repeats each year, the same months will have similar daylight next year.
So you can predict next year's daylight by looking at this year's pattern for the same months.
solution.answer: Because the yearly pattern repeats, you can predict next year's daylight from this year's pattern.

items.prompt: Why is making a graph of shadow lengths more useful than just writing the numbers in a list?

steps: A list of numbers is hard to interpret at a glance.
A graph shows the shape of the data, so rising and falling trends are easy to see.
This makes the pattern, such as the shortest shadow near noon, clear and easy to predict from.
solution.answer: A graph makes the pattern easy to see, so you can spot and predict trends that a plain list hides.
